    Present, Partial or Absent against the printed anchors, write the Panel B row numbers that evidence the mark
    (a mark with no rows is an opinion), name one accountable person and give the date Partial or Absent becomes Present.
    Then write the count of Panel B rows marked &ldquo;In heads&rdquo; in the instrumentation debt box. This sheet records
    present state only: no projected returns, no improvement rates.

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    <b>Panel B &mdash; convention register. One row per convention.</b> Pass 1: spend 30 minutes, whole team in the room, writing
    every convention, pattern and constraint a new engineer would need in their first two weeks. Do not filter. Do not organise
    &mdash; use sticky notes, then transcribe here (ch12 L420). Pass 2: mark where each lives
    today. Pass 3: mark failure cost. Pass 4: mark the target primitive type. Pass 5: tick three to five rows as the starter set, then
    write each file path and a named owner. Number each row; Panel A cites the numbers. Use further copies of this sheet until the register is complete.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Panel B &mdash; convention register <span class="ws-block-note">one row per convention &middot; the five passes are the five fillable columns &middot; the three greyed rows are exemplars from the chapter</span></h2>

      <div class="prior" style="font-size:7.4pt;padding:1mm 2mm"><b>Agent visibility (field 9):</b> In code &rarr; <b>partially visible</b>, if it is in the context window. In docs &rarr; <b>invisible</b> unless explicitly loaded. In heads &rarr; <b>completely invisible</b>.<span class="prior-src">ch12 L435-437</span></div>
      <div class="prior" style="font-size:7.4pt;padding:1mm 2mm"><b>Failure cost (field 10):</b> <b>Critical</b> &mdash; security, data corruption, outages. <b>High</b> &mdash; architectural violations that accumulate as debt. <b>Medium</b> &mdash; convention violations requiring rework at review. <b>Low</b> &mdash; style preferences that do not affect correctness.<span class="prior-src">ch12 L440-445</span></div>
      <div class="prior" style="font-size:7.4pt;padding:1mm 2mm"><b>Primitive type (field 11) &mdash; if the knowledge&hellip;</b> is a rule scoped to files/directories &rarr; instruction file &middot; needs specialist expertise or a specific model &rarr; agent configuration &middot; applies across files and needs a decision framework &rarr; skill &middot; defines a repeatable multi-step process &rarr; prompt &middot; records a decision, trade-off or historical fact &rarr; memory file &middot; specifies a feature with components and success criteria &rarr; specification &middot; defines an automated response to a development event &rarr; hook<span class="prior-src">ch12 L447-457</span></div>
    </div>

    &middot; Panel B absorbs the instrumentation audit, <code>handbook/ch12-the-instrumented-codebase.qmd</code> L418-463

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    <b>Panel C &mdash; technical debt register. Complete and date it before any scenario is chosen.</b> The two or three engineers who have
    been on the codebase longest list the load-bearing modules, one per row; a tech lead with commit history settles which are genuinely
    load-bearing. Write the workaround humans learned in prose (field 20) &mdash; that cell <i>is</i> the context investment, and
    &ldquo;see the team&rdquo; is not an answer. In field 21 write concrete agent failures, or <i>none observed yet</i>. If no module is load-bearing, write <i>none</i> and the reason.
  </div>
